title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants
summary: Whole-roadmap revision of the prismatic roadmap. This packet follows the two accepted parts, PrismaticCohomology--PR.0 (layers PR.0–PR.7, 290 targets) and PrismaticCohomology--PR.8 (79 targets), and adds the thirteen targets the whole-roadmap pass found missing: general prismatic envelopes over an orientable prism (PR.0); Laurent relative Frobenius on Čech nerves (PR.1); initial prisms of quasiregular quotients of a bounded prism (PR.2); quasi-coherent complexes on prestacks, their flat descent, flat affine direct image and the complete-module comparison on formal affines (PR.5); framed q-automorphisms, q-derivations with their Koszul complex and its completed infinite-coordinate form, and the completeness and decay of framed algebras over flat bases (PR.6); and the Beilinson fibre square and Fargues–Fontaine slope-zero named inputs (PR.7). The atlas builds the roadmap from all three packets: scripts/blueprints.py takes the nodes of every promoted packet of a roadmap, and a dry assembly of the three gives 382 declarations, 54 planets and no skipped links. Restructure R1–R6 checks, node by node, the prerequisite edits that move the accepted parts off LanglandsParameterStacks, QWittVectors, RefinedTraceMethods and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals and off bare stage citations, and routes them to the part packets that own those nodes; applied together in a simulation they leave the 382-node graph acyclic. Open: the formal-QCoh comparison outside regular charts, decay on q-PD envelopes with infinite framings, and the proofs behind the two named inputs. All nine stages are planned in the sense of Protocol §0: their targets are present in the accepted parts or here, and unresolved proof and routing obligations remain named. Complete describes this planning pass, not independent acceptance or mathematical closure.

nodes.title: General prismatic envelopes over an orientable prism
nodes.statement: Fix an orientable prism (A,I), with I=(d), without a boundedness assumption. For any delta-A-algebra B and ideal J containing IB, construct a prism (C,IC) and a delta-map B→C carrying J into IC, initial among such maps to prisms over (A,I). Thus precomposition gives a bijection from prism maps C→T over A to delta-A-maps f:B→T satisfying f(J)⊆IT. No regularity, finite generation, completeness or flatness of B or J is assumed. The output is not asserted bounded or completely flat. The resulting functor on delta-pairs is independent of the chosen orientation up to its unique universal isomorphism.
hypotheses: p is prime; (A,I) is orientable; d is a chosen generator for the construction. Both the base and target prisms may be unbounded.
Work in classical set theory with choice and a universe containing A and B; take products in a larger universe if necessary. The zero ring is allowed.

Derived completeness is imported from DD.1/derived-completeness. For a discrete A-module T, its telescope criterion identifies derived (p,d)-completeness with bijectivity of Δ_f:T^N→T^N, Δ_f(x)_n=x_n−f·x_(n+1), for f=p,d. These solution operations are proof devices, not a new definition of generic completion.
proofSteps: By prism rigidity, every target prism over (A,I) has ideal dT and d is a nonzerodivisor. The relation p∈(d,φ(d)) is inherited from A. Thus an ordinary delta-A-ring with d injective and derived (p,d)-complete already gives a target prism.

For f=p,d and each n, let S_(f,n):T^N→T be coordinate n of the inverse of Δ_f in a complete target T. An A-map between two such rings preserves S: applying the map to the equations produces a solution in the target, and bijectivity gives uniqueness. A delta-stable subring closed under all these countably-ary operations is complete; products are complete coordinatewise. Both subrings and products preserve d-injectivity.

Put κ=max(aleph_0,|A|,|B|) and λ=κ^aleph_0. Then λ^aleph_0=λ and λ≥aleph_1. In any admissible map B→T, start with its image and the unique elements y_j satisfying d·y_j=f(j) for j∈J. Close under ring operations, delta and all S_(f,n), successively for omega_1 stages. Every stage and their union have cardinality at most λ. Every countable tuple in the union appears together before some countable stage, so its solutions belong to the next stage. The union T_0 is therefore complete, d-injective and delta-stable. It is a target prism of size at most λ through which B→T factors, still carrying J into dT_0.

The structures on subsets of a fixed set of cardinality λ form a set. Take one representative of each admissible small target together with its A- and B-maps; the preceding closure shows these are a solution set for every B→T. Their product U, with the diagonal map from B, is complete and d-injective. Each j∈J has a unique coordinatewise quotient by d in U. The zero target makes this a nonempty family even when no nonzero target exists.

Inside U, close the diagonal image of B and these quotients under ring operations, delta and all S_(f,n), again for omega_1 stages. Call the resulting subring C. The same countable-cofinality argument proves completeness; d-injectivity and the prism relation are inherited. In particular C is an ordinary discrete ring throughout, so no discreteness assertion about an intermediate derived completion is needed.

For any admissible B→T, choose its small factor T_0, identify a representative in the product, and restrict that product projection to C. This gives C→T. Any two delta-A-maps C→T agreeing on B agree on the unique d-quotients of J and preserve every S_(f,n). Transfinite induction over the generating closure makes them equal. This proves the required bijection, not just existence of a weakly initial object.

Use the universal property for functoriality, identity and composition, independence of orientation, and comparison with regular-prismatic-envelopes. Boundedness and complete flatness transfer only when the independent regular-envelope hypotheses hold. No nonorientable-base descent statement is included.
acceptance: The smallness proof includes all countable solution operations and uses omega_1 rather than omega, so a countable tuple from the final ring has a common earlier stage.
Every map into a complete target preserves the solution operations by uniqueness; this proves uniqueness for the generated ring without making these operations extra morphism data.
The universal property includes unbounded bases and targets. Neither a nonregular exactified kernel nor general existence implies complete flatness or bounded output.

nodes.title: Relative Frobenius on Laurent Čech nerves
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, k a commutative ring of characteristic p, S any set, G=⊕_(s∈S) Z and B=k[G]. Write B^n=B^(⊗_k(n+1)) for the Čech nerve of k→B, and B^{•,(1)}=B^•⊗_(k,Frob_k)k for its relative Frobenius twist. For every cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module N, the natural map N→N⊗_(B^{•,(1)})B^• induces a quasi-isomorphism of unnormalized cochain complexes of k-modules. The tensor product here is degreewise ordinary tensor; each relative-Frobenius map is free. Neither finiteness of S nor flatness of N over k is assumed.
hypotheses: Choose a basis of the free abelian group G. No assertion is made for arbitrary nonfree abelian groups or monoids with p-torsion.
Relative Frobenius fixes the coefficient k after twisting; it multiplies group exponents by p. It is not the absolute Frobenius on the coefficients.
proofSteps: Refine the proof of BS22 Lemma 5.4, pp.48–49, with M=G instead of a free nonnegative monoid. Let T be the finitely supported basis-coordinate vectors with entries in {0,...,p−1}. Every g∈G has a unique expression ph+a with h∈G and a∈T, including negative coordinates. The zero representative makes T a pointed set and T→G/pG a pointed bijection.

In cosimplicial degree n, split each of the n+1 group coordinates by this expression. This identifies k[E(pG)]⊗_k k[ET] with k[EG] as semicosimplicial k[E(pG)]-modules; a coface inserts the zero coordinate, so respects representatives. The relative Frobenius identifies B^{•,(1)} with k[E(pG)]. The comparison map becomes id_N⊗η, where η:k→k[ET] selects the zero representative. The decomposition need not respect codegeneracies, which add coordinates; only cofaces enter the unnormalized differential.

Through T≅G/pG, the semicosimplicial module k[ET] is the underlying semicosimplicial module of the Čech nerve C^• of k→k[G/pG]. The augmentation k[G/pG]→k sending every group element to 1 is a section of the coefficient inclusion. Its split augmented Čech nerve gives a cosimplicial homotopy equivalence k→C^•. Tensoring this homotopy degreewise with any cosimplicial k-module N preserves it, without a flatness assumption. Thus id_N⊗η induces a quasi-isomorphism of the unnormalized complexes.

For infinite S, the same representatives and homotopy are defined directly: every group element has finite support and each Čech degree has only n+1 group coordinates. No reduction of an arbitrary coefficient module N to a finite-variable submodule is assumed. This supplies precisely the ordinary Laurent Čech step used in Koshikawa Appendix B, Lemma B.4, pp.61–62; the log Cartier-type exactness and homotopy assertions remain with the PR.8 consumer.
acceptance: For S empty, B=k and relative Frobenius after twisting is the identity; the comparison is the identity on N.
For G=Z, p=2, the negative exponent −1 decomposes as 2·(−1)+1, so X^(−1)=X^(−2)X. Representatives must allow Laurent exponents in the coefficient group pG.
For p=2, a codegeneracy sends the pair of representatives (1,1) to 2, which is outside {0,1}; a claimed cosimplicial basis decomposition is false, while the semicosimplicial decomposition suffices.
The split homotopy applies to nonflat coefficients, for instance k=F_p[ε]/(ε²) and constant N=k/(ε) with all group variables acting as 1. A proof requiring k-flat N would not meet the statement.

nodes.title: Initial prisms of quasiregular quotients of a bounded prism
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and let A/I→S be a surjection, where S is derived p-complete with bounded p-power torsion and the derived p-completion of L_{S/(A/I)}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. Then Δ_{S/A} is a discrete delta-A-algebra, its reduction modulo I is p-completely faithfully flat over S, and (Δ_{S/A},IΔ_{S/A}) is a bounded prism initial among all prisms over (A,I) equipped with S→B/IB, including unbounded target prisms. If I=(d) and K=ker(A→S), its universal property identifies it with the general envelope of (A,K). No complete-flatness or regular-sequence hypothesis on the original K is required, and no absolute initiality or independence of the arbitrary base A is asserted.
hypotheses: p is prime. The prism (A,I) is bounded, but it need not be perfect or orientable. Orientation is used only for the last comparison with the general-envelope target.

The map A/I→S is surjective as a map of ordinary rings. S is derived p-complete and has bounded p-power torsion. The shifted completed cotangent complex is a p-completely flat S-module in degree zero; these notions are imported from DD.0 and DD.1.

The target category is the unbounded relative prism category. Its morphisms preserve the fixed A-map and the map from S; the result does not assert an initial prism among maps from S with no fixed A-structure.
proofSteps: The derived Hodge–Tate comparison gives gr_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}=Γ_S^i((L_{S/(A/I)}[−1])^∧_p){−i}^∧_p. These are p-completely flat discrete S-modules. The increasing conjugate filtration, its degree-zero unit, and bounded p-torsion give a discrete, p-completely faithfully flat Δ̄ with the same bound on p-power torsion. The discrete-case construction of derived-agrees-with-site supplies a delta-structure on Δ, a bounded prism, and a natural idempotent e_S whose image is the initial object of the category containing all target prisms. It remains to prove e_S is the identity.

Choose generators f_j for ker(A/I→S). Put S′=((A/I)⟨X_j^{1/p^∞} | j∈J⟩/(X_j−f_j | j∈J))^∧_p. Sending every X_j^{1/p^n} to zero gives S′→S. The p-completed cotangent complex of the perfected polynomial extension is zero, and the relation classes map onto the conormal module of S. Consequently the map on shifted completed cotangent complexes is surjective modulo p, and L_{S/S′} has no terms in degrees greater than −2 after derived reduction modulo p. Both rings satisfy the quasiregular hypothesis. The conjugate filtration gives a surjection Δ_{S′/A}→Δ_{S/A}: on each divided-power graded piece use the surjection of flat modules modulo p, then use derived completion. This is the argument of BL22 Remark 4.1.20, not a claim that an arbitrary surjection of rings induces a surjection on Δ.

Naturality gives e_S∘u=u∘e_{S′} for the surjection u:Δ_{S′/A}→Δ_{S/A}; hence e_{S′}=id implies e_S=id. Express S′ as a derived p-completed filtered colimit of the finite-coordinate rings T=((A/I)⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_i−f_i))^∧_p. Colimit preservation of Δ and naturality reduce e_{S′}=id to the same assertion for every T.

For finite T, set A′=(A[X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}])^∧_{(p,I)} with delta(X_i^{1/p^n})=0. This is a bounded prism over A; its reduction is the p-completed perfected polynomial extension of A/I. That extension is p-completely formally étale. The cotangent triangle and the conjugate graded pieces therefore show Δ_{T/A}→Δ_{T/A′} is an equivalence, compatible with delta and the natural idempotents (BL22 Corollary 4.1.17). This is invariance under this specific base extension, not arbitrary invariance under changing the prism.

Choose lifts of the finitely many f_i in A. In A′/IA′ the relations X_i−f_i are Koszul-regular: at every finite root level X_i=(X_i^{1/p^n})^{p^n}, they are successive monic polynomials in distinct variables. Their quotients are free over A/I at that level. Flat filtered passage to all roots and derived p-completion preserve the exact Koszul calculation; the quotients are p-completely flat with bounded p-torsion. Thus regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope (BS22 Example 7.9) applies over A′ and proves e_T=id. Its use of complete-flat regular envelopes occurs only after passing to the universal oriented prism of that existing target's proof. It makes no regularity assertion about the original K.

The preceding reductions prove e_S=id and therefore initiality even for unbounded target prisms. For an orientable A, maps from (A,K) into a prism over A are precisely maps from S into its reduction. The general-envelope universal property gives the unique comparison isomorphism. Boundedness here comes from the Hodge–Tate calculation, not from general-envelope existence.
acceptance: The contract treats arbitrary bounded base prisms, whereas qrsp-prism assumes an A_inf base and proves the stronger absolute initiality specific to a perfect base.
In the reduction, verify surjectivity on the shifted cotangent complex before using surjectivity of Δ; keep the finite-root monic calculation and naturality of the idempotent explicit.

The log consumer identifies its log complex with the ordinary relative complex over the exactified bounded prism by log base change. Only then apply this ordinary theorem, with its actual cotangent-complex and bounded-torsion hypotheses.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent complexes on a prestack
nodes.statement: Let CRing be the category of commutative rings, and let X be a prestack: a functor from CRing to ∞-groupoids (for the uses here, to groupoids, such as Cart, WCart, WCart^HT, Spf A, BG for an affine group scheme G). Its category of points Pt(X) has objects the pairs (R, η) with η ∈ X(R), equivalently morphisms η : Spec R → X, and morphisms (R, η) → (R′, η′) the ring maps f : R → R′ with an identification X(f)(η) ≃ η′. Let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules with derived tensor product, and f^* = R′ ⊗^L_R (−) : D(R) → D(R′). The ∞-category of quasi-coherent complexes on X is the limit D(X) := lim_{(R, η) ∈ Pt(X)} D(R), formed in symmetric monoidal ∞-categories. An object F assigns to each point η a complex F_η ∈ D(R) and to each morphism an equivalence R′ ⊗^L_R F_η ≃ F_{η′}, with all higher coherences. Properties: (1) D(Spec R) ≃ D(R), F ↦ F_{id}; for the terminal prestack Spec Z, D(Spec Z) ≃ D(Z). (2) A morphism g : X → Y of prestacks induces a symmetric monoidal, exact, colimit-preserving pullback g^* : D(Y) → D(X), (g^*F)_η = F_{g∘η}, with id^* = id and (h∘g)^* ≃ g^* ∘ h^*. (3) D(X) is stable and admits small colimits, computed pointwise; it is presentable when X is a small colimit of corepresentable prestacks. (4) D sends small colimits of prestacks to limits: D(colim_i X_i) ≃ lim_i D(X_i). (5) A morphism of D(X) is an equivalence if and only if it is one at every point. (6) The unit O_X is (R, η) ↦ R; Perf(X) ⊂ D(X), the full subcategory of F with every F_η perfect, is exactly the subcategory of dualizable objects, and the invertible objects are those with every F_η invertible in D(R).
hypotheses: Fix nested universes and an essentially small ring/point indexing category in the universe used to form the limit. For a large prestack enlarge the universe; presentability is asserted in that universe only for a small colimit of representables. All rings in this node are ordinary commutative rings.

The limit is a limit of ∞-categories, not of the triangulated homotopy categories: gluing data must include all higher coherences, and the homotopy category of D(X) is not the limit of the homotopy categories of the D(R).

For a functor X defined only on rings in which p is nilpotent (a formal prestack over Spf Z_p, such as WCart), Pt(X) is formed over those rings; this is the same as D of the extension of X by the empty groupoid on the other rings, since the empty prestack has D = 0 (test below).
proofSteps: Construction: apply the straightening of the coCartesian fibration of pairs (R, M ∈ D(R)) over CRing to Pt(X), and take the ∞-category of coCartesian sections; equivalently the right Kan extension of R ↦ D(R) along the Yoneda embedding (Lurie, SAG Definition 6.2.2.1 and Remark 6.2.2.2, with Remark 6.2.2.7 for the pointwise description). The limits of presentable symmetric monoidal ∞-categories used are those of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability/limits-of-presentable-categories.
(1): Pt(Spec R) has the initial object (R, id), so the limit is evaluation there (SAG Remark 6.2.2.5); Spec Z is the terminal prestack because every ring receives a unique map from Z.

(2): precomposition of the limit diagram along Pt(X) → Pt(Y) (SAG Notation 6.2.2.6); (3): every D(R) is stable with colimits and every base change preserves them, so the limit is computed in the subcategory of stable ∞-categories with colimits and colimit-preserving functors (SAG Proposition 6.2.3.4 (1)–(3)).

(4): the right Kan extension of a functor turns colimits of presheaves into limits (SAG Lemma 6.2.1.12 as used in Proposition 6.2.3.1). (5): equivalences in a limit of ∞-categories are detected on the components.

Dualizability is detected componentwise in a limit of monoidal infinity-categories (HA Proposition 4.6.1.11, p.620). In D(R), finite sums, shifts, cones and retracts of R are dualizable. Conversely the duality formula for mapping out of M makes a dualizable M compact, and HA Proposition 7.2.4.4, p.1263 identifies compact modules with perfect modules. The module enhancement and scalar-change action are supplied by E1; its explicit duality comparison is a requested interface, not a consequence of the ordinary DerivedCategory name alone. Invertibility is likewise detected componentwise.
acceptance: For X = Spec R the construction returns D(R), and pullback along Spec R′ → Spec R is derived base change.
For X = WCart it returns Bhatt–Lurie's D(WCart) of Definition 3.3.1, with O_WCart the unit of Example 3.3.3.

For the classifying stack B(Z/2) over F_2 (the quotient of Spec F_2 by the trivial action of the constant group Z/2), Hom_{D(B(Z/2))}(O, O[1]) ≅ H^1(Z/2, F_2) = F_2, while the pullback to the atlas Spec F_2 kills it.

nodes.title: Complete modules on bounded-prism formal affines
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p and a bounded prism (A,I), and put J=(p)+I. Define Spf(A)(R) to be the set of continuous ring maps A→R when R has the discrete topology: equivalently, maps killing J^n for some n. Let D(Spf A) be the pointwise quasi-coherent infinity-category of PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-prestacks, on ordinary rings. There is a natural equivalence E_A:D(Spf A)≃D(A)^∧_J, where the right side is the full enhanced derived category of derived J-complete A-modules, with no cohomological boundedness restriction. Its inverse sends M to the family R⊗^L_A M at A→R. Under this equivalence the unit is A, tensor is M⊗̂^L_A N:=Λ_J(M⊗^L_A N), and colimits are Λ_J(colim_i M_i), where the inner colimit is formed in D(A). For a map of bounded prisms f:(A,I)→(B,IB), pullback corresponds to M↦Λ_(p,IB)(B⊗^L_A M). These equivalences respect identities, composition, units and tensor products, including all higher coherence. This is a formal-affine comparison, not an arbitrary nonflat ordinary-fibre-product base-change theorem. More generally, for any commutative ring R and ideal J generated by a finite regular sequence, the prestack Spf_J R of ring maps R→S with nilpotent image of J satisfies D(Spf_J R)≃D(R)^∧_J, with inverse M↦(S⊗^L_R M)_(R→S), tensor unit Λ_J R, completed tensor Λ_J(M⊗^L_R N) and completed colimits Λ_J(colim M_i); for a transversal prism this applies to the Hodge–Tate chart (A/I,(p)).
hypotheses: The prism is bounded: A/I has bounded p-power torsion. The bounded-prism comparison is not extended here to an individual unbounded prism. I is an invertible Cartier ideal; one may work locally with I=(d).

D(A) and its completion are enhanced infinity-categories imported from E1 and DD.1. Ordinary adic completion of modules and the triangulated category alone are insufficient. Use the universe convention of the prestack construction.

For prism maps, rigidity identifies the target ideal with IB, hence the target topology is the one generated by the image of J. The displayed scalar-change formula is for these compatible ideals. A point A→R has nilpotent image of J, so no further completion is imposed on R⊗^L_A M.

The proof below establishes the unrestricted complex range when J has a finite regular generating sequence, including crystalline prisms I=(p) and transversal prisms locally with regular sequence (d,p). The remaining proof gap is the general bounded-prism case outside this regular-ideal range; the statement above retains BL22’s full bounded-prism target.

The general regular-ideal clause does not assume that R is J-complete. Its tensor unit is Λ_J R, which is R precisely when R is derived J-complete. A bounded prism is already derived (p,I)-complete, so the prism clause has unit A.
proofSteps: The bounded-prism equivalence is stated before BL22 Proposition 3.3.5, p.43, with its boundedness warning 3.3.6. The ordinary-ring prestack Spf A is colim_n Spec(A/J^n), so its quasi-coherent category is lim_n D(A/J^n) with derived transitions. The following argument proves effectivity for a regular generating sequence, without a noetherian hypothesis or a bound on complexes. It does not prove the general nontransversal case.

Suppose J=(f_1,...,f_r) is generated by a regular sequence, r>=1. Set B_n=A/(f_1^n,...,f_r^n). These rectangular ideals are cofinal with J^n: J^(r(n-1)+1) is contained in (f_i^n), which is contained in J^n. The Koszul resolution makes each B_n perfect of uniform A-Tor amplitude [-r,0]. Let M_n be a compatible system, meaning B_n tensor-derived over B_m with M_m is M_n for m>=n, and let M=Rlim_n M_n. Each M_n, and hence M, is derived J-complete by DD.1.

For n>=k let E_(n,k) be the fibre of B_n tensor-derived over A with B_k -> B_k, as a B_n-module. Resolving B_n by the Koszul complex on f_i^n shows that E_(n,k) has cohomology only in [-r,-1]; its degree -j cohomology is the j-th exterior power of B_k^r for 1<=j<=r. The transition from m to n is induced by the Koszul map whose degree-one generators are multiplied by f_i^(m-n). Thus it kills every cohomology group of E when m-n>=k.

All coefficient maps from levels at most m can be restricted to D(B_m). For objects in a fixed interval of r cohomological degrees, r composable maps vanishing on cohomology have zero composite: if the common top degree is b, the first map factors through truncation <=b-1 of its target, the next restricted map factors through truncation <=b-2, and after r maps the target truncation is zero. These factorizations follow from the t-structure orthogonality and the zero map on the current top cohomology. Consequently E_(n+rk,k) -> E_(n,k), the composite through r steps of size k, is zero in D(B_(n+rk)). This is a uniform statement in the derived category, stronger than pro-vanishing of individual Tor groups.

Tensor that zero coefficient map with M_(n+rk) and use the system’s derived scalar-change equivalences. It follows that the tower M_n tensor-derived over B_n with E_(n,k) is uniformly pro-zero, without truncating M_n. Its derived limit vanishes. Since B_k is A-perfect, tensor with B_k commutes with Rlim; the fibre sequences then identify B_k tensor-derived over A with M with M_k. This proves the counit on every compatible, possibly two-sided unbounded system. For a complete M, the unit is DD.1’s Koszul completion formula M=Rlim_n(B_n tensor-derived over A with M). These constructions and maps are in the enhanced categories, so give mutually inverse functors, including their mapping spaces.

For the crystalline prism (A,(p)), p is regular and J=(p), so r=1 applies. For an oriented transversal prism, d is regular and A/d is p-torsion-free, so (d,p) is a regular sequence and r=2 applies. Local orientations are reconciled by descent and the intrinsic reduction functor. No regularity assertion is made for (d,p) over a nontransversal bounded prism. The argument uses only the regular sequence, not the prism structure, so it gives the general regular-ideal clause; for a transversal prism p is regular on A/I, which gives the Hodge–Tate chart (A/I,(p)) with r=1.

Use DD.1/derived-completion and completion-exchanges for the reflective complete category, its completed colimits and tensor. SAG Corollary 8.2.4.15 and Remark 8.2.4.16, p.650 identify spectral formal QCoh with complete modules; Corollary 8.2.4.22 and Notation 8.2.4.23, pp.651–652 give completed tensor. They corroborate these operations but do not by themselves identify the ordinary-ring pointwise category used here. In the general R,J clause, apply the reflector to the ordinary unit R to obtain Λ_J R; at every nilpotent test ring R→S its reduction is S, so this is the structure sheaf under the equivalence. For the empty regular sequence J=0, Spf_0 R=Spec R and the comparison is the usual affine one.

Do not use SAG Theorem 8.3.4.4, pp.667–668 to discharge unbounded ordinary-ring effectivity: it compares connective spectral formal complexes, with almost-connective extension in Corollary 8.3.4.6. Remark 8.3.4.5 explicitly leaves the unrestricted spectral comparison open. The bounded-prism assertion in BL22 is the source for the stronger range in this node.

In this proved range, evaluation at all nilpotent ordinary test rings detects equivalences. DD.1 completion preserves reductions, and derived scalar-change associativity gives the completed pullback and tensor formulas for maps between these charts. The evaluation construction is symmetric monoidal and functorial before taking the limit, so its natural equivalences carry all coherence; it is not enough to choose unrelated triangulated isomorphisms. The reflective complete category gives completed colimits. The same formulas for an arbitrary bounded nontransversal chart remain part of the stated proof gap.

For use in the WCart Cech presentation, combine this comparison with BL22 Lemma 3.3.10 and Corollary 3.3.11, p.44. The completed tensor transition formula is stated in the paragraph between them. Affineness of prism charts is Corollary 3.2.9, p.42; flatness for bounded prisms is equivalent to transversality by Corollary 3.2.10, pp.42–43. Keep that distinction when applying the separate flat affine pushforward theorem.

nodes.title: Faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent complexes
nodes.statement: (1) Let R → S be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings, with Čech nerve S^• (S^n = S ⊗_R ⋯ ⊗_R S, n + 1 factors). Base change gives an equivalence of symmetric monoidal ∞-categories D(R) ≃ Tot(D(S^•)) = lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} D(S^n). (2) Consequently, for a morphism of prestacks u : X′ → X that becomes an equivalence after fpqc sheafification (in particular the canonical map X′ → (X′)^fpqc, with X = (X′)^fpqc), u^* : D(X) → D(X′) is an equivalence. (3) If X is an fpqc stack and U → X is a morphism of prestacks that is an effective epimorphism of fpqc sheaves (surjective fpqc-locally), with Čech nerve U_• (U_n the (n + 1)-fold fibre power over X), then D(X) ≃ Tot(D(U_•)); the same holds with the Zariski topology in place of the fpqc topology when U → X is a Zariski-local surjection. (4) On the hearts, (1) restricts to faithfully flat descent of modules.
hypotheses: (1): R → S faithfully flat, so every S^n is a discrete ring and every coface map is flat; for non-flat R → S the statement is false (test: Z → F_p).
(3): X is an fpqc (respectively Zariski) stack of ∞-groupoids on commutative rings; the fibre powers U_n need not be affine.

Use the universe convention of the construction node. Sheafification and effective epimorphisms of space-valued prestacks require the infinity-categorical extension requested from D0; its present groupoid stackification alone does not supply it.
proofSteps: (1) is the case of discrete rings and flat maps of Lurie's fpqc descent for module ∞-categories (SAG Corollary D.6.3.3); flatness keeps the Čech nerve discrete, so the relative tensor products agree with the ordinary ones.

(2): D sends colimits of prestacks to limits (PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-prestacks (4)); by (1) the functor Spec R ↦ D(R) is an fpqc sheaf of ∞-categories, so D factors through fpqc sheafification (the argument of SAG Proposition 6.2.3.1 and Remark 6.2.3.2).

(3): an effective epimorphism of sheaves is the geometric realization of its Čech nerve, so X ≃ |U_•| after sheafification; apply (2) and the limit property (4) of the construction node. This is the descent step of Bhatt–Lurie Lemma 3.3.10 (Zariski) and of the proof of Proposition 3.3.5 (flat).
(4): truncate to discrete objects and compare with SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent.
acceptance: For X = WCart and the Zariski surjection Spf(A^0) → WCart with fibre powers Spf(A^n), (3) gives Bhatt–Lurie's equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot(D̂(A^•)) (Lemma 3.3.10). Here D(Spf A) is the derived (p,I)-complete module category, not D(A). The displayed transversal Čech charts have regular defining ideals, so formal-affine-complete-qcoh supplies their formal-affine identification and completed scalar change. The all-bounded-prism version remains the recorded nonregular formal-QCoh gap.
For a finite Galois extension of fields K → L with group G, (1) and (3) give D(K) ≃ D(L)^{hG}, the ∞-categorical form of Galois descent.
Non-example: for Z → F_p (not flat), Tot(D(F_p^{⊗•})) is not D(Z); for instance Q is killed by base change.

nodes.title: Flat affine direct image, base change and projection formula
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a flat affine morphism of prestacks on ordinary commutative rings: each fibre Y ×_X Spec R is Spec B_η with B_η flat over R, and ordinary pullback gives B_η ⊗_R R′. Then (a) f^* has a right adjoint f_*, whose value at η is the restriction to Spec B_η regarded as an R-complex; (b) g^* f_* ≃ f′_* g′^* for every base change g : X′ → X; and (c) f_* preserves small colimits and F ⊗ f_*G ≃ f_*(f^*F ⊗ G). These three assertions are about flat affine maps in this discrete-prestack setting. Independently, (d) if D(X) is presentable in the chosen universe, M ↦ M ⊗ O_X from D(Z) to D(X) has a right adjoint RΓ(X,−). For an effective fpqc or Zariski Čech presentation, RΓ(X,F) is the totalization of the global sections of its restrictions. On formal affine charts, use derived complete module categories and completed tensor products under the separately recorded formal-QCoh interface.
hypotheses: Each B_η is flat over R. Without this, an ordinary pullback B ⊗_R R′ need not compute B ⊗^L_R R′. SAG uses spectral prestacks and derived fibre products, so its arbitrary base-change theorem is not an arbitrary ordinary-ring base-change theorem.

For (d), presentability and the universe bound are hypotheses, not automatic assertions for every large prestack. On the formal Čech presentation of WCart, use the complete module categories of BL22 Lemma 3.3.10 and Corollary 3.3.11.
proofSteps: For R → B flat, B ⊗^L_R R′ = B ⊗_R R′, so associativity identifies R′ ⊗^L_R M with (B ⊗_R R′) ⊗^L_B M. The restrictions of G to affine fibres therefore form a Cartesian family of R-complexes. The adjunction is the limit of these coherent pointwise scalar-extension/restriction adjunctions.

Pointwise restriction of scalars preserves colimits and satisfies the projection formula. Evaluation detects the resulting equivalences. SAG Proposition 6.3.4.1 and Corollary 6.3.4.3, pp.505–507, supply the derived setting; flatness permits this discrete specialization.

For (d), apply the presentable adjoint theorem to the colimit-preserving tensor-with-unit functor. Under Čech descent mapping spaces and the pointwise global-section adjunctions identify its right adjoint with the totalization. This argument does not require the atlas maps U_n → X themselves to be affine. BL22 Corollary 3.3.11 gives the WCart instance.
acceptance: For a bounded transversal prism, ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart is flat affine (BL22 Corollary 3.2.10, pp.42–43). The flat affine theorem applies on ordinary-ring points; its expression in complete A-modules additionally uses the formal-QCoh interface. Affineness of an arbitrary bounded prism is insufficient for the pointwise base-change claim.
For WCart, BL22 Corollary 3.3.11 computes RΓ as Tot(M^•) on its universal oriented-prism Čech presentation, with a derived p-complete result.

nodes.title: Framed algebras and their q-automorphisms
nodes.statement: Put t = q − 1 in a commutative coefficient ring D and I = (t) or (p,t). Let P be an ordinary D-algebra, classically and derived I-complete, with an I-completely ind-étale polynomial or toric framing D[X_s]^∧_I → P. Require that the completed framing source is discrete, that P/tP and P/(tX_s)P are classically I-complete, and that every tX_s is a nonzerodivisor. Then there are unique D-algebra automorphisms γ_s that scale X_s by q, fix the other coordinates and reduce to the identity modulo t. They commute, and γ_s(f) − f belongs to tX_sP. Continuous D-algebra maps with an injective coordinate map intertwine these automorphisms; automorphisms in extra target directions fix the image. If D and P are p-torsion-free, P/pP is classically I-complete, D is a δ-ring with δ(q)=0, and I=(p,t), P has the unique compatible δ-structure with δ(X_s)=0, and its Frobenius commutes with the γ_s. These are sufficient hypotheses for the completed variant, rather than a claim about all merely p-completely ind-étale framings. The completion topologies used by the sources are compared by the following cofinal-power formulas: J=(p,[p]_q)⊆K=(p,q−1), K^(p−1)⊆J; for q=(1+u)^p and ξ=[p]_(1+u), K⊆H=(p,ξ) and H^p⊆K.
hypotheses: All coefficient automorphisms are D-linear and hence fix q. Polynomial completion is taken at I; in the toric variant the coordinates are units. Modulo every I^n the framing is ind-étale.

Classical completeness of P and the listed quotients is imposed so reduction and compatible infinitesimal lifts recover actual maps and principal-ideal divisibility. It is not inferred from the words derived complete alone. Extending this sufficient formulation to every general-base consumer remains a gap.
The parameter q is a unit in the I-completed framing source and in P because t ∈ I; D itself need not be complete or contain q^(−1).
The δ assertion needs p-torsion-freeness of P as well as D, and classical I-completeness of P/pP to detect divisibility by p after infinitesimal lifting. I contains p and φ(t)=q^p−1 belongs to I.

For prime p and t=q−1 in any commutative ring, put J=(p,[p]_q) and K=(p,t). Then J⊆K and K^(p−1)⊆J, hence K^((p−1)n)⊆J^n⊆K^n for every n. For u with q=(1+u)^p and ξ=[p]_(1+u), put H=(p,ξ). Then t=uξ, K⊆H and H^p⊆K, hence H^(pn)⊆K^n⊆H^n. These are cofinal ideal filtrations, not equal ideals. They identify the classical completions of every module and the corresponding continuous maps. For derived completion, use DD.1/ordinary-quotient-completion only after verifying its regular-sequence or other comparison hypotheses for both ideals. In A_inf(O_C), u=[ε^(1/p)]−1 and ξ generates ker θ; both p and the nonzero reductions of u,t,ξ are regular, so the regular-pair comparison applies. This argument neither gives a merely p-adic framing nor proves completeness of P/(tX_s).
proofSteps: On the completed polynomial algebra scale one coordinate by q. The inverse scales it by q^(−1), which exists in the completed source. The difference on a monomial is divisible by tX_s; the same formula holds on toric monomials.

For each n, ind-étaleness modulo I^n lifts the identity modulo I uniquely along the nilpotent I/I^n thickening, with the changed polynomial structure map. Take the compatible limit in the classically I-complete algebra P. Applying the same uniqueness modulo t proves reduction to the identity. Uniqueness proves commutation and the inverse formula. This is the completed-lifting argument of SQDEF §3, pp.6–7, with the extra quotient-completeness hypotheses stated here.

To obtain divisibility, repeat uniqueness in P/(tX_s,I^n), where the altered coordinate map is the identity. Completeness of P/(tX_s) identifies the inverse limit with this quotient, so γ_s acts as the identity there. For coordinate-injective maps compare the two induced lifts; an extra target direction has the unchanged polynomial map, hence fixes the image.

For the δ assertion, put the framed Frobenius on the source: φ_D on coefficients and X_s↦X_s^p. Modulo I this is Frobenius; since φ(I)⊆I, unique ind-étale infinitesimal lifting extends it through each P/I^n and then to P. Compare modulo (p,I^n) with the characteristic-p Frobenius; completeness of P/pP gives φ_P(f)≡f^p modulo p. Dividing by p in the p-torsion-free P gives the unique δ-structure (PR.0/delta-ring-category). Its compatibility with the source and γ_s follows from δ(q)=δ(X_s)=0 and uniqueness of the same lifts. The ordinary delta-etale-extension node motivates this argument but is not being asserted to supply the completed extension without these hypotheses.

The topology comparison is elementary: modulo p, [p]_q=t^(p−1). Thus J⊆K and every degree-(p−1) monomial in p,t lies in J. In the cyclotomic case the geometric-sum identity gives t=uξ, while modulo p one has t=u^p and ξ=u^(p−1), so ξ^p=t^(p−1) modulo p and H^p⊆K. Raise these inclusions to powers. Cofinal inverse systems give the classical module-completion comparison. For A_inf, p-torsion-freeness and the domain O_C^♭ identify the two generating pairs as regular; invoke the stated DD.1 ordinary-quotient comparison for derived completions. The identities compare topology only; do not transport a regular quotient or an ind-étale framing without checking it.
acceptance: For P = D[X]^∧ with one coordinate, γ(X^m) = q^m X^m for m ≥ 0.
Modulo q − 1 every γ_s is the identity, so all structure collapses to the plain framed algebra P/(q − 1).

nodes.title: q-derivatives and the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex
nodes.statement: Let D → E be a map of commutative rings, q ∈ D, X_s ∈ E and γ_s commuting D-algebra automorphisms with γ_s(X_t)=q^(δ_st)X_t, γ_s(f)−f ∈ (q−1)X_sE, and each (q−1)X_s a nonzerodivisor. For any set S, the unique quotients ∇_(q,s) defined by (q−1)X_s∇_(q,s)(f)=γ_s(f)−f are D-linear, obey the twisted Leibniz law, satisfy ∇_(q,s)(X_s^n)=[n]_q X_s^(n−1) for n≥1 and commute pairwise. For finite S their cochain Koszul complex has qΩ^i = E ⊗_D Λ^i(D^S), in degrees 0 through |S|, and differential fω ↦ Σ_s ∇_(q,s)(f)dX_s∧ω. It is linear over the common γ-invariants. For infinite S the separate completed-q-derivative-summability target gives a construction under an explicit decay condition; verifying decay for every inherited consumer remains a gap. A coordinate-injective D-algebra map gives a chain map if it intertwines matching γ_s and all extra target directions fix its image. For a finite complete étale framing as in the previous node, with flat coefficients and the completed reduction identified with the framed special fibre, reduction modulo q−1 is its continuous relative de Rham complex. For unit coordinates the change of basis dX_s = X_s dlog X_s identifies the complex with the Koszul complex of (γ_s−1)/(q−1), hence with η_(q−1) of the complex of γ_s−1. Finally, if φ commutes with γ_s, φ(q)=q^p and φ(X_s)=X_s^p, then ∇_(q,s)φ=[p]_q X_s^(p−1)φ∇_(q,s).
hypotheses: The automorphisms fix the coefficient ring D, including q. For qΩ impose finite S, or the separately specified continuity and summability conditions; the exact quotient operators alone impose no summability.
For a map with coordinate injection j:S→S′, require hγ_s=γ′_(j(s))h and γ′_u h=h for u outside j(S). Injectivity alone is insufficient for arbitrary q-derivation data.

For reduction use finite completely étale framed algebras flat over a t-torsion-free coefficient ring. The differential forms are continuous and completed at the image of I; when I=(p,t), the special-fibre forms are p-completed. The complete formal differential interface is requested explicitly.
proofSteps: Divide by the regular element tX_s to get the unique quotient. D-linearity uses γ_s(a)=a for a∈D. Expand γ_s(fg)−fg to prove twisted Leibniz. The monomial formula follows from q^n−1=t[n]_q. For s≠u, both γ_s and γ_u fix t and the other coordinate; multiply the two iterated derivatives by t^2X_sX_u, use commutation of γ_s and γ_u, and cancel this regular product. For equal indices commutation is tautological.

For finite S form the finite cochain Koszul complex of these commuting D-linear endomorphisms; paired wedge signs give d²=0. This is the commuting-endomorphism interface requested from AI.1, not the existing scalar-sequence Koszul DGA and not an automatic ordinary commutative DGA product. Infinite completed sums require the separate summability gap.

Use uniqueness of the regular quotient to intertwine the matching derivatives. The extra-direction fixed-image condition kills all additional differential terms, so the induced wedge map is a chain map.

Check the infinitesimal automorphism modulo t²: it induces X_s times the ordinary partial derivation. Unique infinitesimal lifting along the étale framing identifies this on P. Dividing first and then reducing gives the continuous partial derivatives and the completed de Rham complex. The identity γ_s≡1 modulo t by itself does not identify the divided quotient; use the first-order calculation (BS22 Construction 16.19, footnote 21, p.114).

For unit coordinates use dX_s=X_s dlog X_s. The differential γ_s−1 is divisible by t, so the degree-i submodule of η_t of its Koszul complex is exactly t^i times the degree-i term; multiplication by t^i identifies the divided-operator complex with it. This directly establishes the required special case of the AI.1 décalage construction. For Frobenius apply φ to the quotient equation and cancel tX_s, using φ(tX_s)=t[p]_q X_s^p.
acceptance: For the Laurent chart E=Z[T^(±1)][[t]], q=1+t, use the logarithmic basis and the derived t-completion of the direct sum of two-term blocks Z[q,q^(−1)] --[n]_q--> Z[q,q^(−1)] indexed by n∈Z. The n=0 block has zero differential and contributes the constant and dlog T classes. For n<0 define [n]_q=(q^n−1)/(q−1). This is an equality of completed complexes; no interchange of H¹ with ordinary completion of a direct sum of torsion modules is asserted.
For P=Z[X][[t]] with its t-complete framing, reduction gives Z[X] → Z[X]dX with the ordinary derivative. For an I=(p,t) framing use continuous p-completed special-fibre forms.
The Frobenius identity (6) for f = X: ∇(X^p) = [p]_q X^{p−1}.

sources.match: Defines the q-derivative as the finite q-difference quotient (γ_i(f) − f)/(qT_i − T_i), computes it on monomials as the q-integer times the lower power, forms the framed q-de Rham complex, and records that it reduces modulo q − 1 to the de Rham complex.

nodes.title: Summability of q-derivatives in completed coordinate modules
nodes.statement: Let E be a classically I-adically complete separated D-algebra, with I a finitely generated ideal of D, and let (q,X_s,γ_s)_(s∈S) be the regular q-derivation datum of q-derivations-and-their-koszul-complex. Require the decay condition: for every f∈E and n≥1, ∇_s(f)∈I^nE for all but finitely many s. Define completed q-forms in degree i as lim_n ⊕_(F⊂S finite, |F|=i) (E/I^nE)e_F, using an auxiliary total order for wedge signs. They form a cochain complex with d(f e_F)=Σ_s ∇_s(f)e_s∧e_F, independent of the order by the canonical exterior-basis change. Finite S recovers the finite Koszul complex, because E is complete. A continuous D-algebra map with an injective coordinate map intertwining matching γ_s and fixed image under extra target γ_u induces a chain map of completed complexes. A sufficient criterion for decay is: some c≥0 satisfies (I^(n+c)E:tX_s)⊆I^nE uniformly in s,n≥1, and for every f,n the differences γ_s(f)−f lie in I^(n+c)E for all but finitely many s. Here t=q−1. The standard completed polynomial and Laurent charts over Z[[t]] with I=(t), or Z_p[[t]] with I=(p,t), satisfy this criterion with c=1. No assertion that every completed ind-étale algebra or q-PD envelope satisfies it is made without verification.
hypotheses: I is pulled back from D. D-linearity implies ∇_s(I^nE)⊆I^nE uniformly in s, so each induced quotient operator is well-defined. Individual continuity without decay is insufficient.

The completed forms use the inverse-limit topology with kernels of projection to level n. No assertion that arbitrary ordinary quotients of a complete module are complete is used. The complex is D-linear; a usual commutative DGA product is not asserted.

For standard charts, first establish the uniform colon estimate from injectivity of multiplication by the initial form of tX_s in the associated graded ring. A general change of coefficient ring requires rechecking that estimate.

AI.1 owns the generic commuting-operator complex and its completion interface. This target checks the q-specific convergence contract and charts; it does not create a second generic Koszul theory. DD.2 continuous forms are used only in their stated finite smooth range.
proofSteps: Regular division gives the q-operators and their pairwise commutation by the preceding target. At level n, decay makes d(f e_F) a finite sum, and D-linearity makes it independent of the chosen lift of f modulo I^n. Extend linearly to the finite-support degree-i module. The two orders of every distinct pair of operators cancel by their wedge signs, while repeated indices wedge to zero. Thus d_n²=0, including in characteristic two. The quotient operators commute with transition maps; take the degreewise inverse limit. No interchange of cohomology with inverse limit is used.

The algebraic exterior module is dense in these completed forms. The differentials preserve each projection kernel, so the formula extends uniquely and continuously. For finite S each degree has finitely many basis vectors and completion returns the finite Koszul terms over E.

For maps, regular-quotient uniqueness intertwines matching derivatives; extra-direction fixed-image hypotheses make the additional terms zero. At every quotient level the induced wedge map takes finite support to finite support. Pass to the inverse limit, obtaining identity and composition compatibilities.

For the sufficient criterion, divide γ_s(f)−f=tX_s∇_s(f) using the uniform colon inclusion. In a standard polynomial or Laurent chart, approximate f modulo I^(n+1) by a polynomial with finitely many coordinates. Every other γ_s fixes that approximation. The associated graded ring is Z[X_s][T] for I=(t), or F_p[X_s][P,T] for I=(p,t), with coordinates inverted in the Laurent case. Multiplication by TX_s is injective and raises filtration by one, proving (I^(n+1):tX_s)⊆I^n uniformly. Completeness and separatedness exclude an element of infinite nonzero filtration order.

For a completed ind-étale or q-PD-envelope consumer, verify finite-coordinate approximation and a uniform division estimate, or prove decay directly on a dense generating family. The later theorem framed-algebras-over-flat-bases supplies these estimates for completely ind-étale polynomial framings over a base flat over Z_p[[q−1]], for every coordinate set. The q-PD-envelope and monoid-chart verifications remain in the complete-framing gap. Regularity of each tX_s alone supplies no uniform estimate.

api.name: QFraming.completedQDeRham_finite

api.name: QFraming.completedQDeRham_map

api.name: QFraming.polynomial_qDeriv_decay

tests.statement: For S empty, completed degree zero is E, every positive degree is zero and d=0. For finite S, agreement with the finite Koszul complex is degreewise, not merely an agreement of cohomology.

tests.statement: Let E=Z[Y,X_s^(±1):s∈N][[t]], D=Z[[t]], q=1+t. Let γ_s scale both X_s and Y by q and fix the other X_u. These are continuous commuting D-algebra automorphisms with regular tX_s and differences divisible by tX_s. But ∇_s(Y)=Y/X_s for every s, nonzero modulo t, so the derivative tuple does not belong to the completed direct sum. The missing étale framing of Y is essential; abstract regular q-data alone do not imply decay.

nodes.title: Framed algebras over flat bases satisfy the completeness and decay hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let A=Z_p[[t]] with t=q−1, and I=(p,t). Let D be a derived I-complete A-algebra that is flat over A, S any set, and P a derived I-complete D-algebra with an I-completely ind-étale framing D[X_s:s∈S]^∧_I→P, meaning that P is I-completely flat over the framing source and that every ordinary reduction P/I^nP is ind-étale over (D/I^n)[X_S]. Then: (1) P is discrete and classically I-complete, and gr_I P≅(P/IP)[p̄,t̄]; p, t, every X_s and every tX_s are nonzerodivisors on P, and X̄_s is a nonzerodivisor on P/IP. (2) The quotients P/pP, P/tP and P/tX_sP are classically I-complete, so P satisfies the sufficient hypotheses of framed-q-automorphisms for I=(p,t), its δ-clause included when D is a δ-ring with δ(q)=0. (3) Uniformly in s∈S and n≥0, (I^(n+1)P:tX_s)⊆I^nP. (4) For every f∈P and n≥0 there is a finite F⊆S with γ_s(f)≡f modulo I^(n+1)P for all s∉F, hence ∇_s(f)∈I^nP for s∉F. Thus P satisfies the decay condition of completed-q-derivative-summability with c=1, and its completed q-de Rham complex exists for every S. Nothing is asserted about q-PD envelopes of P or about monoid-algebra charts.
hypotheses: D is flat over A, as for the framed q-PD data of BS22 §16. Derived (p,[p]_q)-completeness is the same condition as derived I-completeness, because the two ideals have cofinal powers (framed-q-automorphisms).

I-completely ind-étale is taken in the convention of framed-q-automorphisms: the derived reduction of P modulo I is discrete and ind-étale over (D/I)[X_S], and every ordinary reduction modulo I^n is ind-étale over (D/I^n)[X_S].
No finiteness of S and no noetherian hypothesis on D or P is assumed. A is noetherian, but the argument uses only the associated graded ring and Tor vanishing over A.
proofSteps: Complete flatness over A. D is flat over A, so I-completely flat; the completed framing source D[X_S]^∧ has reduction (D/I)[X_S], free over D/I; P is I-completely flat over the source. Composing, P⊗^L_A N is discrete for every I-power-torsion A-module N (DD.1/complete-flatness).

Discreteness and classical completeness. By the Koszul completion tower of DD.1 the derived completion of P is Rlim_n P⊗^L_A A/(p^n,t^n), since (p^n,t^n) is regular on A. These Koszul reductions are the discrete modules P/(p^n,t^n)P, with surjective transitions, so P≅lim_n P/(p^n,t^n)P. The filtrations by (p^n,t^n) and by I^n are cofinal, so P is classically I-complete and separated.

Associated graded ring. Tor_1^A(P,A/I^n)=0 makes I^n⊗_A P→P injective with image I^nP, and Tor_1^A(P,I^n/I^(n+1))=0 gives I^nP/I^(n+1)P≅(I^n/I^(n+1))⊗_(A/I)P/IP. Hence gr_I P≅F_p[p̄,t̄]⊗_(F_p)P/IP=(P/IP)[p̄,t̄].

Regular elements and colon estimates. P/IP is ind-étale, hence flat, over (D/I)[X_S], on which X_s is a nonzerodivisor; so X̄_s is a nonzerodivisor on P/IP. Let g∈P have initial form of degree e that is a nonzerodivisor on gr_I P. If x∈I^mP∖I^(m+1)P, the initial form of gx is the product of the two initial forms, which is nonzero, so gx∉I^(m+e+1)P. Since P is separated, g is a nonzerodivisor and (I^kP:g)⊆I^(k−e)P. Apply this to p, t (e=1), X_s (e=0, initial form X̄_s when P≠0) and tX_s (e=1, initial form t̄X̄_s in the polynomial ring). The case tX_s is (3).

Closed quotients. For g∈{p,t,tX_s}, step 4 gives I^kP∩gP=g·I^(k−e)P, so the subspace topology on gP is the I-adic topology of gP≅P. Then gP is complete, hence closed in the separated module P, and P/gP is separated and complete for the quotient topology, which is its I-adic topology. This proves (2): P and its framing source are discrete and classically and derived complete, P/tP and P/tX_sP are classically complete, tX_s is regular; for the δ-clause, D and P are p-torsion-free and P/pP is classically complete.

Finite-coordinate approximation. Put C=D/I^(n+1). The algebra P/I^(n+1)P is a filtered colimit of étale C[X_S]-algebras. Choose a piece and an element representing the image of f. Finite presentation descends the piece to an étale C[X_F]-algebra E_F for finite F⊆S. Enlarge F to include every additional variable appearing in the chosen element of E_F⊗_(C[X_F])C[X_S]; after this enlargement f is in the image of E_F itself. For s∉F, the structure map E_F→P/I^(n+1)P and its composite with γ_s are C[X_F]-algebra maps, because γ_s fixes C and X_F. They coincide modulo I, since γ_s reduces to the identity on P/IP. Formal étaleness makes lifts through the nilpotent kernel of P/I^(n+1)P→P/IP unique (Algebra.FormallyEtale). Hence the two maps agree and γ_s(f)≡f modulo I^(n+1)P. Including the variables in the element is essential: descent of the étale presentation alone does not imply this conclusion.
Decay. For s∉F, tX_s∇_s(f)=γ_s(f)−f lies in I^(n+1)P, so ∇_s(f)∈I^nP by (3). This is the sufficient criterion of completed-q-derivative-summability with c=1.

Scope. Flatness of D over A is used in step 1 and the polynomial framing in steps 4 and 6. The argument does not reach q-PD envelopes D_(J,q)(P), which are not ind-étale over a polynomial ring, nor the monoid-algebra charts of PR.8/log-q-de-rham-complex.
acceptance: For D=A and P=A[X_S]^∧ with S infinite, the theorem recovers the polynomial-chart decay of completed-q-derivative-summability with c=1.
Flatness of D cannot be dropped: for D=A/(t)=Z_p, t acts by zero on P, so tX_s is not a nonzerodivisor and no q-derivative is defined.

The common-Y example continuity_not_decay of completed-q-derivative-summability is outside the theorem: its γ_s are not the automorphisms determined by an ind-étale polynomial framing, since Y is not étale over the coordinates.
No decay is claimed for q-PD envelopes or for log charts.

nodes.title: The Beilinson fibre square on syntomic complexes (named input)
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R write Q_p(n)(R) = Z_p(n)(R)[1/p] for the syntomic complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex, LΩ_R for the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of R over Z_p with its Hodge filtration LΩ_R^{≥n} (not Hodge-completed), and (−)_{Q_p} for p-completion followed by inverting p. (i) For every p-torsion-free quasisyntomic ring R and n ≥ 0 there are a natural map χ_n : Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p), left column Q_p(n)(R) → (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}, right column χ_n and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}. (ii) For R quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free and n > 0, χ_n is injective with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; up to a nonzero scalar depending only on n it is the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] composed with Δ_{R/p} ≅ A_crys(R/p) ≅ LΩ_R. (iii) Check: for R = O_C the sequence on H^0 is 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 for n ≥ 1. Within this roadmap the statement is a named input: its only consumer, PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, is proved from it, and its proof (through topological cyclic homology) lies outside the roadmaps this roadmap builds on.
hypotheses: R p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic in (i); quasiregular semiperfectoid in (ii); n ≥ 0 in (i), n > 0 in (ii).
The order of operations in (−)_{Q_p} matters: complete first, then invert p.

This roadmap does not prove the statement: the proof constructs the square from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) over HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) and the motivic filtrations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, which no roadmap below this one in the upstream order provides; the gap 'Trace-theoretic proof of the Beilinson fibre square' records it.

Quasisyntomic includes p-adic completeness and bounded torsion as in DD.5. AMMN qSyn_Zp here is the p-torsion-free subcategory. A_crys(R/p) ≃ LΩ_R and the comparison between trace-defined and prismatic syntomic objects are interfaces recorded as gaps until supplied in this tier.
proofSteps: Outline of the source proof, for the record of the named input: for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the bottom row of the TC/HC^-/HP square is even, so τ_{[2n−1, 2n]} of the square is again a pullback; by the definition of Z_p(n) through the motivic filtration and the description of π_{2n}HC^- and π_{2n}HP by Hodge-completed derived de Rham cohomology this gives a Hodge-completed version of the square; Hodge completion is removed by left Kan extension from polynomial algebras; general quasisyntomic R follows by unfolding (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 with proof).

(ii): Proposition 6.18 of the same paper, using Corollary 6.20, the Frobenius action of Lemma 6.19 and the scalar-endomorphism argument of Proposition 6.21; the identification of their Z_p(n) (defined with topological cyclic homology) with the prismatic syntomic complex is Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 14.1 with Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Theorem 1.12.

(iii): for R = O_C, Q_p(n)(O_C) = Q_p(n)[0] by the étale comparison PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, Q_p(n)(O_C/p) has H^0 = (A_crys(O_C/p)[1/p])^{φ = p^n} = (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} and LΩ_{O_C}/Fil^n ⊗ Q = B_dR^+/Fil^n (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4/rational-hodge-period-comparison).
acceptance: For R = O_C and n = 1: 0 → Q_p(1) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p} → C → 0, the fundamental exact sequence.
For n = 0 the third term vanishes and the square says Q_p(0)(R) ≃ Q_p(0)(R/p).
Consumed exactly once: PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, steps 2–3.

nodes.title: Triviality of the slope-zero bundle of a weakly admissible module (named input)
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of characteristic zero with perfect residue field k, C the completion of a chosen algebraic closure of K, F=C^♭ and E=Q_p. Let X_sch be the schematic Fargues–Fontaine curve of F with the untilt point ∞ determined by C, and ℛ the Robba ring of FF Definition 1.8.1. The named input comprises: (i) vector bundles on X_sch correspond to Frobenius-equivariant analytic bundles on Y through GAGA (FF Theorem 11.3.1), and these correspond to finite free ℛ-modules with invertible semilinear φ (Corollary 11.2.22); (ii) for a weakly admissible filtered φ-module D over K_0=W(k)[1/p], with D_K=D⊗_(K_0)K, the modification of E(D) at ∞ defined by the B_dR^+-lattice Fil^0(D_K⊗_K B_dR) is semistable of slope zero (Proposition 10.5.6); and (iii) every slope-zero semistable bundle on X_sch is O_(X_sch)^r (Theorem 8.2.10(1)). Consequently its Robba φ-module has a φ-fixed basis. Transport to the adic quotient curve supplied by AdicSpaces requires the analytic/schematic dictionary, point ∞, Robba-ring normalization and construction matching specified in the gap. These are named inputs for PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf, rather than a supplied classification theorem of AdicSpaces.
hypotheses: C is the completed algebraic closure of K in the source of the weak-admissibility assertion; the algebraically closed tilt is essential for the slope classification.

Use the usual filtered φ-module convention D_K=D⊗_(K_0)K and N=0. The Frobenius-twisted scalar convention of the prismatic consumer must be matched explicitly, not identified silently. R06.2 presently has a finite-extension field range; its perfect-residue-field extension is a precise supplier request.

The schematic curve, its untilt point and bundles are part of this named interface. AdicSpaces supplies only the adic quotient construction. GAGA and compatibility of the period modification with the particular Robba module of the consumer remain recorded proof/construction gaps.
proofSteps: Use FF Theorem 11.3.1 (pp.330–331) to pass from schematic bundles to analytic Frobenius-equivariant bundles, then Corollary 11.2.22 (p.328) for the Robba-module equivalence. Specify the radius normalization and tensor-compatible dictionary in the supplier interface.

FF Proposition 10.5.6 (p.290), under the Chapter 10 setup (p.264), identifies the Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of the filtered module and its modified bundle. Weak admissibility gives slope zero. FF Theorem 8.2.10(1) (p.238) then trivializes this schematic bundle.

Under the equivalence the trivial rank-r bundle is the rank-r module with its standard φ, so it has a φ-fixed basis. To use this on PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf one must identify that consumer’s analytic continuation with this modification; BS23-FCRYS §6.4 p.26 asserts the matching and the inherited packet already records its proof as a gap.
acceptance: For D = K_0 with φ_D = σ and the trivial filtration, the bundle is O_X and the φ-module is ℛ with its Frobenius: trivially trivial.

For D = D_cris(V) of a crystalline representation V (for instance V = Q_p(1), D = K_0 e with φ(e) = p^{-1}e and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0), the modified bundle is V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X, trivial of slope 0, as (ii)–(iii) predict.

consumerProofAdjustment: For S=1+pB, first replace B by B_loc=S^(-1)B and B/J by B_loc/JB_loc, leaving M_B→N unchanged. The multiplicative set S is Frobenius-stable since φ(1+pb)=1+pφ(b), so the delta-log structure extends uniquely by PR.0/delta-localization-criterion. The image of p lies in the Jacobson radical of B_loc: if x=b/s with s∈S, then s+pb∈S, so 1+px is a unit.

Every target prism T is derived (p,I)-complete, hence p lies in its Jacobson radical; every delta-log map B→T therefore factors uniquely through B_loc. The compatible map B/J→T/IT also factors through B_loc/JB_loc. Thus the original universal problem is unchanged, without requiring classical completeness or boundedness of T.

Apply PR.8/delta-log-groupification (K1 Proposition 2.16, p.11) to M_B⊂M′=(h^gp)^(-1)(N)⊂M_B^gp over B_loc. Put E=B_loc⊗_(Z_(p)[M_B]) Z_(p)[M′] and K=ker(E→B_loc/JB_loc). This gives the same exact-surjective monoid map M′→N.

Now apply general-prismatic-envelope to (E,K) over (A,I). Carry M′, its structure map and its delta-log values along E→C. The resulting (C,IC,M′) is a prelog prism with exact-surjective M′→N. The localization, monoid exactification and ordinary-envelope universal properties successively give existence and uniqueness of lifts to every target, including unbounded prisms. No flatness or boundedness of C is inferred.
